title.en: Why do children look like parents?

text.en: A child may have the mother's nose and the father's eyes. Heredity explains how traits pass from parents to children.

Heredity is the transmission of traits from parents to offspring. Variation is differences among individuals.
Gregor Mendel worked on garden pea plants and studied traits like tall and short, round and wrinkled seeds.
When he crossed a pure tall plant with a pure short plant, all F1 plants were tall. In F2 tall and short appeared in the ratio 3 : 1.
So the tall trait is dominant and the short trait is recessive. Each trait is controlled by a pair of factors, now called genes.
A dihybrid cross of round yellow and wrinkled green seeds gave a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio in F2, showing independent inheritance of traits.
Traits are expressed through proteins made from genes on DNA in chromosomes.
Sex determination in humans: 22 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes. Females are XX and males are XY.
A child's sex depends on the father's sperm: X gives a girl and Y a boy. The chance of a boy or girl is 50 percent each.

problem.en: In a pea cross Tt x Tt, find the ratio of tall to short plants.

text.en: Gametes of each parent: T and t.
Three tall (TT, Tt, Tt) and one short (tt): ratio 3 : 1.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the mother decides the sex

points.en: Monohybrid cross F2 ratio 3 : 1; dihybrid ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
Genes are on DNA in chromosomes.
Males XY, females XX; the father's sperm decides the sex.
